name: Copy consistency
definition: The app says the same thing in different words: one action with different verbs, one concept with different names, one situation with different messages, or a mix of tones and capitalisation. Compare the screen under review with the reference screen.

checklist.question: Is the same action named with different verbs on this screen or against the reference screen (Delete / Remove / Trash, Save / Apply / Done)?
Is one concept called by two names (Project and Workspace, Note and Entry, Team and Group) for the same thing?
Is the same situation (nothing found, saved, failed to load) worded differently than on the reference screen in a way the user would notice?
Does the copy switch tone (formal and casual; 'you', 'we' and 'the user'; playful and dry) within the screen or against the reference?
Do buttons, headings or menu items mix Title Case and Sentence case for the same kind of element?

bad: The list says 'Remove plant' and the detail page says 'Delete plant' for the same action.
The sidebar says 'Gardens'; the page header says 'Plots' for the same thing.
Buttons 'Add Task' and 'Add note' side by side.
good: 'Archive' and 'Delete' both appear: they are different actions.
Every button uses Sentence case: 'Add task', 'Add note', 'Export list'.

severityRubric.medium: the inconsistency is on a core path or about an action with consequences (delete, pay, share)
severityRubric.low: wording or capitalisation drift that does not change what the user understands
